mainTopic: Splitting letters and נוטריקון in the מלאכה of writing, ידיעה for a חצי שיעור, and the start of the new chapter on the minimum amounts for weaving, sewing and tearing.
overview: This amud opens with a quick קשיא and תירוץ. Someone who splits one letter into two is חייב only if the new letters do not still need their crowns (זיונין). Next comes the מחלוקת about writing one letter as a נוטריקון: רבי יהושע בן בתירה holds him חייב and the חכמים hold him פטור. The גמרא then gives a long list of נוטריקון readings to show that the Torah really uses abbreviations: אב המון, אנכי, ירט, כרמל, נמרצת and נצטדק. A new משנה follows about two letters written in two separate העלמות. The גמרא explains that רבן גמליאל and the חכמים argue over whether awareness (ידיעה) divides a חצי שיעור. After the הדרן for פרק הבונה, a new chapter opens with the minimum amounts for weaving, making loops, sewing and tearing. The גמרא resolves the dispute over 'two' or 'three' threads, quotes two ברייתות and identifies whose view each follows, and defines the loom terms. It then explains why the משנה repeats sewing and tearing: to lead into tearing in anger or for the dead. At the end it asks when one would tear in order to sew, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Splitting a letter into two letters makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ruling: someone who split one letter and ended up with two letters is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and he ended up with two letters in his hand: he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of a ruling. That ruling says a person who split one letter into two letters is חייב for writing on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is someone who divides a single letter so that two separate letters result, for example a ח split into two ז's. The ruling treats this as writing two letters, which is the minimum amount for liability. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: and he ended up with (literally, 'it came up in his hand')
liable to bring a קרבן חטאת

phrases.english: and he ended up with two letters — he is liable.
phrases.notes: The end of a ruling that began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ruling begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Splitting one letter into two letters counts as writing two letters, so the person is חייב.

steps.title: But the משנה says he is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling: the משנה says that in this case the person is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה that he is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ruling just quoted seems to contradict our משנה. The משנה says this person is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is the same: one letter divided into two. Yet one source says חייב and the משנה says פטור. That is a direct contradiction, and the גמרא needs to resolve it.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't we learn (in a משנה)?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: he is exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that splitting a letter into two makes one חייב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules פטור in the same case, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: It depends on whether the letters need crowns
steps.stepSummary: The two sources address different cases. If the new letters still need their crowns, he is פטור. If they don't need crowns, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. That case (exempt) is where the letters still need crowns. This case (liable) is where they do not need crowns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the case in two. Each source is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some letters, such as ז, are written with small crowns (זיונין). If the two new letters still need their crowns added, the writing is incomplete, so he is פטור, as the משנה says. If they don't need crowns, or already have them, he has finished two complete letters and is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: this is not difficult (introduces an answer)
this case... that case... (splits into two situations)
crowns (the small decorative strokes on certain letters)

steps.whatToRemember: Splitting a letter into two makes one חייב only when the resulting letters are complete. If they still need their crowns, he is פטור.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
that one (exempt) is where they need crowns,
this one (liable) is where they do not need crowns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between two cases (אוקימתא of each source).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling and the משנה seemed to be about the identical case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה (פטור) is where crowns are still needed. The ruling (חייב) is where no crowns are needed.

steps.title: The משנה's dispute about writing an abbreviation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if someone writes one letter as a נוטריקון standing for a whole word, רבי יהושע בן בתירה holds him חייב and the חכמים hold him פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone wrote one letter as an abbreviation, רבי יהושע בן בתירה holds him liable and the Sages exempt him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה. That line records a מחלוקת about writing a single letter that stands for a whole word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person must write two letters to be חייב. Here only one letter was written, but it represents a full word. רבי יהושע בן בתירה counts its meaning, so he is חייב. The חכמים count the single letter on the page, so he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: an abbreviation, where letters stand for whole words
the תנא who holds liable here

phrases.english: If he wrote one letter as an abbreviation,
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beteira holds him liable
and the Sages exempt him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת whether one letter written as an abbreviation makes one חייב.

steps.title: The Torah itself uses abbreviations: אב המון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יוסי בן זימרא, shows that נוטריקון appears in the Torah. The words אב המון in the פסוק about אברהם are read letter by letter as six praises.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we see abbreviation language in the Torah? From 'For a father of a multitude of nations I have made you.' I made you a father to the nations, chosen among the nations, beloved among the nations, a king to the nations, distinguished among the nations, and trusted by the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that abbreviation is a real way the Torah speaks. This explains how רבי יהושע בן בתירה can take one letter as meaningful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of אב המון are decoded one by one. א is אב, ב is בחור, ה is חביב (ה and ח swap), מ is מלך, ו is ותיק, and ן is נאמן. Since the Torah uses letters this way, a single letter can stand for a full word.
steps.confusionAlert: The word המון is the second word being decoded, and its letter ה stands for חביב, since ה and ח are treated as interchangeable. Do not read המון as an extra praise.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a Torah basis for treating a single letter as a complete word, which supports the view of רבי יהושע בן בתירה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִימְרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra:
From where do we get abbreviation-language in the Torah?
As it says: 'For a father of a multitude of nations I have made you' —
(א) a father I made you for the nations,
(ב) chosen I made you among the nations,
[the word] 'hamon': (ה/ח) beloved I made you among the nations,
phrases.notes: The ה of המון is read as ח for חביב.

phrases.english: (מ) a king I made you for the nations,
(ו) distinguished I made you among the nations,
(ן) trusted I made you for the nations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a Torah source for נוטריקון, relevant to the משנה's מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: That נוטריקון is a legitimate form of Torah language.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית יז:ה, 'כי אב המון גוים נתתיך'.

steps.title: אנכי as an abbreviation: I Myself wrote and gave
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's own example: the word אנכי at the start of the עשרת הדברות stands for 'אנא נפשי כתבית יהבית'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן himself said: 'אנכי' is an abbreviation for 'I Myself wrote and gave.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another example of נוטריקון, this time רבי יוחנן's own. He reads the four letters of אנכי as four Aramaic words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter matches a word: א is אנא, נ is נפשי, כ is כתבית, and י is יהבית. The message is that ה' personally wrote and gave the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I', the first word of the עשרת הדברות

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan himself said:
'Anochi' is an abbreviation:
I Myself wrote and gave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further example of נוטריקון, from the same אמורא speaking in his own name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אנכי is read as 'אנא נפשי כתבית יהבית'.

steps.title: The Rabbis' reading of אנכי
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read אנכי as 'אמירה נעימה כתיבה יהיבה', a pleasant statement, written and given.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis say: a pleasant saying, written and given.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן offer a different abbreviation for the same word, אנכי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters are the same but the words differ: א is אמירה, נ is נעימה, כ is כתיבה, and י is יהיבה. Here the focus is on the Torah's pleasant words rather than on ה' personally writing it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis say:
a pleasant saying, written and given.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative decoding of the same word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אנכי is read as 'אמירה נעימה כתיבה יהיבה'.

steps.title: Reading אנכי backwards
steps.stepSummary: Some read אנכי in reverse: 'יהיבה כתיבה נאמנין אמריה', given, written, its words are trustworthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say 'אנכי' is read backwards: it was given, it was written, its words are trustworthy.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion decodes אנכי from the last letter to the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read backwards, the letters are י־כ־נ־א: י is יהיבה, כ is כתיבה, נ is נאמנין, and א is אמריה. This shows that a נוטריקון can even work in reverse order.

phrases.english: Some say 'Anochi' read backwards:
given, written, trustworthy are its words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of אנכי, this time in reverse order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אנכי read backwards gives 'יהיבה כתיבה נאמנין אמריה'.

steps.title: ירט: the donkey feared, saw, and turned
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי נתן reads ירט in the בלעם story as an abbreviation for 'יראה, ראתה, נטתה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי נתן say: 'For the way is contrary (ירט) before me': it feared, it saw, it turned aside.
steps.whatsHappening: Another example of נוטריקון, from the story of בלעם's donkey. The odd word ירט is broken into three words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: י is יראה, ר is ראתה, and ט is נטתה (the key letter ט). This describes what the donkey did when it saw the מלאך.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Natan say:
'For the way is contrary (yarat) before me' —
it feared, it saw, it turned aside.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי נָתָן אָמְרִי כִּי יָרַט הַדֶּרֶךְ לְנֶגְדִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another Torah example of נוטריקון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירט is read as 'יראה ראתה נטתה'.

steps.title: כרמל: a full kernel
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that כרמל means 'כר מלא', a full kernel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'כרמל' means 'a full kernel.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another example: one word is split into two words that explain its meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word is divided into two parts, כר and מל, rather than letter by letter. כרמל in ויקרא refers to fresh grain whose kernels fill the stalk.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'Karmel' — a full kernel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another example in the list of נוטריקון.

steps.title: נמרצת: the five insults of שמעי
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב reads נמרצת, the 'grievous curse' שמעי בן גרא cursed דוד with, as an abbreviation for five insults.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: 'He cursed me with a grievous (נמרצת) curse' is an abbreviation: he is an adulterer, he is a Moabite, he is a murderer, he is an oppressor, he is an abomination.
steps.whatsHappening: Another example in the list. Each letter of נמרצת becomes one of the insults שמעי hurled at דוד המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נ is נואף, מ is מואבי, ר is רוצח, צ is צורר, and ת is תועבה. The word 'grievous' is therefore explained as a curse packed with five specific accusations.

keyTerms.meaning: a Moabite (questioning דוד's lineage through רות)

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא lists many examples (אב המון, אנכי, ירט, כרמל, נמרצת, and נצטדק in the next step) to show that נוטריקון is a real form of Torah language. This background explains why רבי יהושע בן בתירה can treat one letter standing for a word as meaningful writing.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
'And he cursed me with a grievous (nimretzet) curse' is an abbreviation:
he is an adulterer, he is a Moabite,
he is a murderer, he is an oppressor,
he is an abomination.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר וְהוּא קִלְלַנִי קְלָלָה נִמְרֶצֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another example in the list of נוטריקון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נמרצת is read as 'נואף, מואבי, רוצח, צורר, תועבה'.

steps.title: נצטדק as an abbreviation for five claims of innocence
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the word נצטדק in יהודה's plea to יוסף as standing for five words: נכונים, צדיקים, טהורים, דכים, קדושים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: "What can we speak, and how can we justify ourselves (נצטדק)" stands for: we are honest, we are righteous, we are pure, we are innocent, we are holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one last example to its list of words that are read as abbreviations. Each letter of the word stands for a whole word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take the letters of נצטדק one at a time: נ־צ־ט־ד־ק. They become נכונים, צדיקים, טהורים, דכים, קדושים. So inside the very word יהודה uses to ask "how can we prove our innocence," the brothers are hinting at five claims that they really are innocent.

keyTerms.meaning: We will justify ourselves / prove our innocence

steps.whatToRemember: This ends the list of abbreviation readings. The list started because the chapter was discussing writing, and how one letter can stand for a whole word.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
"What can we speak, and how can we justify (nitztadak)"
phrases.notes: בראשית מד:טז. These are יהודה's words to יוסף.

phrases.english: we are honest, we are righteous,
phrases.notes: Here נ stands for נכונים and צ for צדיקים.

phrases.english: we are pure, we are innocent,
phrases.notes: Here ט stands for טהורים and ד for דכים.

phrases.english: we are holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final example to the series of abbreviation readings in steps 5–11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נצטדק = נכונים, צדיקים, טהורים, דכים, קדושים.

steps.title: Two letters written with awareness in between
steps.stepSummary: The משנה: someone writes two letters on שבת in two separate lapses of awareness, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. רבן גמליאל holds him חייב and the חכמים hold him פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone writes two letters in two separate lapses of awareness, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. רבן גמליאל holds him liable, and the חכמים exempt him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives a case. A person writes the minimum amount needed to be חייב (two letters), but he writes it in two halves. In between the two halves, he realizes that it is שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two letters is the full שיעור for the מלאכה of כותב, so one letter alone is only half a שיעור. A חטאת is brought for a full מלאכה done בשוגג, within one העלם (one stretch of not knowing). Here the realization in the middle breaks the forgetting into two העלמות, so the question is whether the two halves can still join together.

keyTerms.meaning: A lapse of awareness; forgetting that it is שבת or that the act is forbidden
Holds liable / exempt (here, from bringing a חטאת)

steps.confusionAlert: "Two העלמות" means that he found out it was שבת between the two letters, and then forgot again. That moment of finding out (ידיעה) is the whole issue in this case.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who writes two letters
in two lapses of awareness,
one in the morning and one in the afternoon,
Rabban Gamliel deems him liable
and the Rabbis exempt him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַכּוֹתֵב שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת בִּשְׁתֵּי הֶעְלֵמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic abbreviation series and opens a new halachic case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two letters written in two העלמות: רבן גמליאל says חייב, the חכמים say פטור.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבן גמליאל and the חכמים disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the מחלוקת in the משנה. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only gives the two rulings. The גמרא wants to find the one underlying idea that splits the two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they argue? (a standard question asking for the root of a מחלוקת)

phrases.english: GEMARA: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the מחלוקת in the משנה of step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle underlying the disagreement between רבן גמליאל and the חכמים.

steps.title: Does awareness count for half a measure?
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל holds that awareness does not matter for half a שיעור, so the two letters join together. The רבנן hold that awareness does matter for half a שיעור, so the two letters are split apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל holds: there is no awareness for half a measure. And the רבנן hold: there is awareness for half a measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the whole argument depends on one question. Does a moment of realizing "it's שבת" have any effect when only half the שיעור has been done so far?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a ידיעה between two sins divides them into separate units. רבן גמליאל says a ידיעה only divides things you could bring a קרבן for, and half a שיעור is not one of them. So the first letter is ignored for this purpose, the two letters combine, and he is חייב. The רבנן say the ידיעה divides even halves, so each letter stands alone as only half a שיעור, and he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness; realizing that one has sinned or that it is שבת
Half of the minimum amount needed to be liable
Awareness has no dividing effect on half a measure
Awareness does divide, even for half a measure

steps.confusionAlert: The wording works the opposite way from what you might expect. "אין ידיעה" (no awareness counts) leads to being חייב, because nothing separates the two letters. "יש ידיעה" (awareness counts) leads to being פטור, because the letters are split apart and cannot combine.
steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל: the ידיעה does not split half-measures, so they combine and he is חייב. רבנן: the ידיעה splits them, so he is פטור.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel holds:
there is no awareness for half a measure,
phrases.notes: So the ידיעה in the middle does not separate the two letters.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold:
there is awareness for half a measure.
phrases.notes: So the ידיעה separates the two letters, and they cannot combine.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר אֵין יְדִיעָה לַחֲצִי שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is whether a ידיעה has a dividing effect on a חצי שיעור: רבן גמליאל says no, the רבנן say yes.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הבונה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula of the chapter הבונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, [chapter] הבונה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter הבונה. The next chapter begins after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is a traditional farewell said when finishing a chapter, expressing the hope to return and learn it again. It is not part of the legal argument.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)
"One who builds": the name of the chapter now ending

phrases.english: We will return to you, [chapter] HaBoneh

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final משנה and גמרא.

steps.title: משנה: How many threads of weaving make one liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר: three threads at the start, or one added onto existing cloth, makes one חייב. The חכמים: two threads, whether at the start or the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה. רבי אליעזר says: someone who weaves three threads at the beginning, or one thread onto already-woven cloth, is liable. The Sages say: whether at the beginning or at the end, the amount is two threads.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה about the מלאכה of weaving on שבת. It asks how much weaving makes a person חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר sets two different amounts. Starting a new weave takes three threads, but adding onto cloth that already exists takes only one. The חכמים set a single amount of two threads in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: One who weaves (one of the 39 מלאכות)
The minimum amount that makes one חייב

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who weaves three threads at the beginning
or one onto woven fabric is liable.
And the Sages say:
whether at the beginning or at the end,
its measure is two threads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter right after the Hadran of הבונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: three threads to begin a weave, one thread to add onto existing cloth. חכמים: two threads either way.

steps.title: משנה: Making two loops, sewing two stitches, tearing to sew
steps.stepSummary: Making two loops on the loom parts, a sieve, a sifter or a basket makes one חייב. So does sewing two stitches, and tearing in order to sew two stitches.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who makes two loops on the heddles, on the קירוס, on a sieve, a sifter, or a basket is liable. So is one who sews two stitches, and one who tears in order to sew two stitches.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the minimum amounts for related מלאכות: making loops, sewing and tearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these מלאכות has a set amount of two: two loops or two stitches. Tearing only counts when it is done to make room for sewing, which is a constructive purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Loops or meshes of the heddle (a loom part)
A part of the loom (the גמרא explains it later)

phrases.english: One who makes two loops
on the heddles, on the keiros,
on a sieve, a sifter, or a basket is liable.
And one who sews two stitches,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַקּוֹרֵעַ עַל מְנָת לִתְפּוֹר שְׁתֵּי תְפִירוֹת.
phrases.english: and one who tears in order to sew two stitches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with more weaving-related מלאכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two loops, two stitches, or tearing in order to sew two stitches makes one חייב.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's version: two threads
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יצחק came from ארץ ישראל, he taught that רבי אליעזר's number for starting a weave is 'two', not 'three'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא. When רבי יצחק came, he taught: 'two'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רבי אליעזר's statement that gives the number as two threads. This sets up a clash with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says רבי אליעזר requires three threads to start a weave. רבי יצחק's tradition says two. The next step points out the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: When [a sage] came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
He taught (a version of a teaching)

phrases.english: GEMARA: When Rabbi Yitzchak came,
he taught: 'two'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different wording of רבי אליעזר's view from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יצחק's version, רבי אליעזר's amount for starting a weave is two threads.

steps.title: But our משנה says three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: our משנה clearly says 'three'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: 'three'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's version, because our משנה says three threads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two traditions give two different numbers for the same opinion. One of them seems to be wrong.

phrases.english: But we learned: 'three'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the version brought in step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It contradicts our משנה, which says 'three'.

steps.title: Answer: thick threads versus thin threads
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. One source is talking about thick threads and the other about thin threads.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one is about thick threads, that one is about thin threads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both numbers are correct, because each applies to a different kind of thread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number depends on how thick the thread is. The answer does not yet say which number goes with which kind of thread. The next steps explain that.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is with thick ones, that is with thin ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא בְּאַלִּימֵי הָא בְּקַטִּינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two numbers for one opinion must contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each number applies to a different thickness of thread.

steps.title: First version: what matters is whether the weave holds
steps.stepSummary: There are two versions of how the answer works. In the first, thick threads need three because two would unravel, while thin threads hold even with two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way and some say it that way. Some say it this way: with thick threads, three do not unravel but two do. With thin threads, even two do not unravel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first announces that two versions of the answer exist, which sets up both explanations. Then it gives the first version, which is based on whether the threads stay in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the test is staying power. Thick threads only hold with three, so 'three' (our משנה) is about thick threads. Thin threads hold even with two, so 'two' (רבי יצחק) is about thin threads.
steps.confusionAlert: The two versions match the numbers to opposite thread types. In this first version, thick threads need three. In the second version, thin threads need three. Keep them separate.

phrases.english: Some say it this way,
and some say it that way.
Some say it this way:

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּימֵי — תְּלָתָא לָא סָתְרִי, תְּרֵי סָתְרִי.
phrases.english: Thick ones: three do not unravel, two do unravel.
Thin ones: even two do not unravel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לַהּ לְהַאי גִּיסָא וְאָמְרִי לַהּ לְהַאי גִּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the thick/thin distinction of step 21 works.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reasoning behind the distinction (durability).
steps.terutzMaskana: Three threads applies to thick threads and two applies to thin threads, because that is what holds together.

steps.title: Second version: what matters is whether the weave is noticeable
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, thin threads need three because two cannot be seen, while two thick threads are already noticeable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say it that way: with thin threads, three are noticeable but two are not. With thick threads, even two are noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second version of the answer, which is based on whether the weaving can be seen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the test is visibility, so the numbers flip. Thin threads only show with three, so 'three' (our משנה) is about thin threads. Thick threads show even with two, so 'two' (רבי יצחק) is about thick threads.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that רבי אליעזר's 'three' and 'two' fit different thread thicknesses. They only disagree about which test decides it: holding together or being seen.

phrases.english: And some say it that way:

phrases.aramaic: קַטִּינֵי — תְּלָתָא יְדִיעִי, תְּרֵי לָא יְדִיעִי.
phrases.english: Thin ones: three are noticeable, two are not noticeable.
Thick ones: even two are noticeable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite version of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reasoning behind the distinction (visibility).
steps.terutzMaskana: Three threads applies to thin threads and two applies to thick threads, because that is what can be seen.

steps.title: First ברייתא: weaving threads, a hem, and a small belt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats the dispute from the משנה. It adds that weaving a hem takes two threads across three loops, just like weaving a small belt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: one who weaves three threads at the beginning or one onto woven fabric is liable. The Sages say: whether at the beginning or the end, the measure is two threads. And on a hem, two threads across a width of three loops. What is this like? Like weaving a small belt: two threads across a width of three loops.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that restates the משנה's dispute and adds a rule about weaving a hem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new part is the hem (שפה): two threads across three loops is enough to make one חייב. The reason given is that this already makes a small usable item, like a narrow belt.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Hem or edge of a garment

phrases.english: It was taught: One who weaves three threads at the beginning
or one onto woven fabric is liable.
And the Sages say:
whether at the beginning or at the end,
their measure is two threads.
And on a hem: two threads
across a width of three loops.
To what is this similar?
To one who weaves a small belt:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי חוּטִין בְּרוֹחַב שְׁלֹשָׁה בָּתֵּי נִירִין.
phrases.english: two threads across a width of three loops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that parallels and expands the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weaving a hem is חייב at two threads across three loops, like weaving a small belt.

steps.title: The unattributed opening of the first ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The opening line of the ברייתא has no name attached, and the גמרא identifies it as רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'one who weaves three threads at the beginning or one onto woven fabric is liable' is unattributed, following רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out whose opinion the unnamed first line of the ברייתא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא the first line has no name, and the חכמים argue against it. That line matches what the משנה attributes to רבי אליעזר, so it is his view.

phrases.english: And 'one who weaves three threads at the beginning
or one onto woven fabric is liable'
is unattributed, following Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the ברייתא quoted in step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first ברייתא opens with רבי אליעזר's view stated anonymously.

steps.title: Second ברייתא: two threads on a large fabric or border
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: weaving two threads onto a large fabric or its border makes one חייב. רבי אליעזר says even one thread. A hem takes two threads across three loops, like a small belt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: one who weaves two threads onto a large fabric or onto the border is liable. רבי אליעזר says: even one. And on a hem, two threads across a width of three loops is liable. What is this like? Like weaving a small belt: two threads across a width of three loops.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second ברייתא in which the unnamed opening sets the amount at two threads, and רבי אליעזר disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the order is reversed. The unnamed opinion says two threads, and רבי אליעזר says even one, which fits his view that one thread added onto existing cloth is enough. The hem and belt rule is repeated just as in the first ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The border or edge of a fabric

phrases.english: Another baraita taught:
One who weaves two threads onto a large fabric
or onto the border is liable.
Rabbi Eliezer says: even one.
And on a hem, two threads
across a width of three loops is liable.
To what is this similar?
To one who weaves a small belt:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי חוּטִין עַל רוֹחַב שְׁלֹשָׁה בָּתֵּי נִירִין:
phrases.english: two threads across a width of three loops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא that parallels the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two threads onto a large fabric or border makes one חייב, while רבי אליעזר says even one. A hem takes two threads across three loops.

steps.title: The unattributed opening of the second ברייתא follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the unnamed opening of the second ברייתא as the view of the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'one who weaves two threads onto a large fabric or onto the border is liable' is unattributed, following the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the unnamed first line of the second ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two threads is the amount the חכמים give in the משנה, and here רבי אליעזר argues against it. So this ברייתא opens with the רבנן's view without naming them, which is the reverse of the first ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות mirror each other. In the first, the anonymous opening is רבי אליעזר's view. In the second, it is the רבנן's view. In both, the hem rule is two threads across three loops.

phrases.english: And 'one who weaves two threads onto a large fabric
or onto the border is liable'
is unattributed, following the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the ברייתא quoted in step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second ברייתא opens with the רבנן's view (two threads) stated anonymously.

steps.title: What does 'on the heddles' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about making two heddle-loops and asks what the word בנירים means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who makes two heddle-loops…' What does 'on the heddles' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה and asks for the meaning of an unclear weaving word. This sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists several places where making two loops makes a person חייב, and the first is בנירים. The גמרא wants to know exactly what that action looks like on a loom.

keyTerms.meaning: Heddle-loops: loops on a loom that hold the threads
Heddles: the loom parts that lift and lower threads
Etc.: the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: One who makes two heddle-loops, etc.
What is 'on the heddles'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתות about weaving to the next clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word בנירים in the משנה

steps.title: אביי explains the heddle-loops
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains: two threads go in the heddle-holder and one goes in the heddle itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Two in the heddle-house and one in the heddle.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by describing how the threads are set up when making heddle-loops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The action that makes a person חייב is building these loops on the loom. אביי describes the arrangement: two threads in one part and one thread in the other, which together form the loops.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the משנה here
The 'house' of the heddle: the part holding the loops

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Two in the heddle-house
and one in the heddle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Making heddle-loops means arranging two threads in the heddle-house and one in the heddle

steps.title: What is a קירוס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next word in the משנה, בקירוס, and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On a קירוס.' What is a קירוס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of another unclear loom word in the משנה. This sets up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says making two loops on a קירוס also makes one חייב. The word is unfamiliar, so the גמרא asks for a definition.

keyTerms.meaning: A part of the loom named in the משנה

phrases.english: On a kiros.
What is 'on a kiros'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues defining the משנה's loom words

steps.title: רב defines קירוס
steps.stepSummary: רב says a קירוס is a מצוביתא, a loom part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It is a מצוביתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers by giving the Aramaic name of the loom part the משנה calls קירוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב translates the unclear Hebrew word into a familiar Aramaic word for a part of the loom. One common explanation is that it refers to the slips, the parts that move up and down on the loom.

keyTerms.meaning: A loom part, explained as the slips, the parts that move up and down on the loom

phrases.english: Rav said:
A metzuvita (a loom part).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 30
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קירוס is a מצוביתא, a part of the loom

steps.title: Sewing was already taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: why does our משנה teach sewing two stitches, when the list of אבות מלאכות already taught it?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one who sews two stitches.' But we already learned this in the list of אבות מלאכות: 'and one who sews two stitches'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that our משנה seems to repeat a law that was already taught earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in the seventh perek lists the 39 אבות מלאכות, including 'one who sews two stitches.' A משנה is not supposed to repeat itself for no reason, so why say it again here?

keyTerms.meaning: The 39 main categories of forbidden work on שבת

phrases.english: And one who sews two stitches.
But we already learned in the primary labors:
And one who sews two stitches!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement about sewing two stitches
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It looks like a pointless repeat of the list of אבות מלאכות

steps.title: Sewing is a lead-in to tearing in order to sew
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions sewing only because it wants to go on to teach 'one who tears in order to sew two stitches.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it wanted to teach the later clause, 'and one who tears in order to sew two stitches,' it also taught 'one who sews.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the sewing line is not the real point. It is an introduction to the next line about tearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is the measure for tearing: tearing in order to sew two stitches. To present it neatly, the משנה first mentions sewing as its partner.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause of a משנה

phrases.english: Because it wanted to teach the latter clause:
'And one who tears in order to sew
two stitches,'
it also taught 'one who sews.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32
steps.terutzResolutionType: Repetition explained as a lead-in to a new law later in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sewing line is a pointless repeat
steps.terutzMaskana: It is stated only to introduce tearing in order to sew

steps.title: Tearing was also already taught
steps.stepSummary: The answer fails: tearing in order to sew is also in the list of אבות מלאכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one who tears.' But we also learned this in the list of אבות מלאכות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the last answer. The tearing line is also already in the list of 39 מלאכות, so it cannot be the new idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of אבות מלאכות includes 'one who tears in order to sew two stitches.' So the line that was supposed to justify mentioning sewing is itself a repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: But we also already learned this

phrases.english: And one who tears.
But we also learned this in the primary labors!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 33
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the tearing clause justifies the sewing clause
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tearing is itself a repeat from the list of אבות מלאכות, so it cannot be the new teaching

steps.title: The real new law: tearing in anger or for the dead
steps.stepSummary: The משנה repeats sewing and tearing in order to lead into a truly new law: tearing in anger or for a dead relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because it wanted to teach the later clause, 'one who tears in his anger or for his dead,' for that reason it taught 'one who sews two stitches.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. The whole sewing-and-tearing section is a lead-in to a law that does not appear in the list of מלאכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing in anger or for a dead relative is the new law in our משנה. To reach it, the משנה first repeats the basic laws of sewing and tearing, and then adds this new case.

keyTerms.meaning: For his dead relative (קריעה for mourning)

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה repeats sewing and tearing from the list of אבות מלאכות only to lead into its new law: tearing in anger or for a dead relative.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה is teaching sewing or tearing for the first time here. Those lines are review that set up the new case.

phrases.english: Rather, because it wanted to teach the latter clause,
one who tears in his anger or for his dead,
for that reason it taught
[one who sews two stitches].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 33 after the challenge in step 34
steps.terutzResolutionType: Repetition explained as a lead-in to a truly new later clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tearing in order to sew is the new point
steps.terutzMaskana: The new point is tearing in anger or for the dead, and the earlier lines lead into it

steps.title: When would someone tear in order to sew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'one who tears in order to sew two stitches' and asks what real case this describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one who tears in order to sew two stitches.' Where do you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the case itself. The answer, which describes a realistic case, comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally people tear things to destroy them, not to fix them. The גמרא wants to know when tearing actually helps sewing, which would make it a constructive act that brings חיוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Where do you find this case?

phrases.aramaic: וְהַקּוֹרֵעַ עַל מְנָת לִתְפּוֹר שְׁתֵּי תְפִירוֹת.
phrases.english: And one who tears in order to sew two stitches.
Where do you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from why the clause is repeated to what real case it describes
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic case where tearing is done for the sake of sewing
